title: Use R to Write LaTeX Code in R Markdown Documents
text: following example demonstrates approach. Consider following equation, encountered Riemannian geometry: ddt⟨V,W⟩=⟨DVdt,W⟩+⟨V,DWdt⟩ \frac{d}{dt} \left \langle V,W \right \rangle = \left \langle \frac{DV}{dt}, W \right \rangle + \left \langle V, \frac{DW}{dt} \right \rangle traditional LaTeX implementation : Using latexSymb, equation can constructed programmatically. Begin creating objects class latex_symb represent vector fields: Next, define R functions represent mathematical operations: inner product, covariant derivative, ordinary derivative: Finally, combine elements within equation environment: d⟨V,W⟩dt=⟨DVdt,W⟩+⟨V,DWdt⟩\begin{equation}\frac{ d \langle V , W \rangle }{ dt } = \langle \frac{ D V }{ dt } , W \rangle + \langle V , \frac{ D W }{ dt } \rangle\end{equation} Note: Use cat rather print prevent display escaped backslashes.
code: \frac{d}{dt} \left \langle V,W \right \rangle = \left \langle \frac{DV}{dt}, W \right \rangle + \left \langle V, \frac{DW}{dt} \right \rangle library(latexSymb) ## Loading required package: purrr ##  ## Attaching package: 'latexSymb' ## The following objects are masked from 'package:base': ##  ##     -, *, /, ^, + data(common) attach(common) ## The following object is masked from package:base: ##  ##     pi vf1 <- lsymb("V") vf2 <- lsymb("W") inner <- function(x, y) ang(lsymb(x, ",", y)) cov.der <- function(x) lsymb("D", x) / "dt" ddt <- function(x) lsymb("d", x) / "dt" lenv(   "equation",   lsymb(     ddt(inner(vf1, vf2)),     eq,     inner(cov.der(vf1), vf2) + inner(vf1, cov.der(vf2))   ) ) |> cat()

title: Use R to Write LaTeX Code in R Markdown Documents
text: approach utilizes several key features latexSymb package. definition cov.der demonstrates operator overloading latexSymb. / operator redefined either argument latex_symb object, returns new latex_symb object using appropriate \frac command. Similar overloading implemented +, -, *, ^ operators. function provides subscript functionality. numerator cov.der, lsymb("D", x) concatenates string "D" object x, returning new latex_symb object. ang function automatically handles delimiter sizing angle brackets, eliminating need explicit \left \right commands. Similar functionality provided br (braces), sqbr (square brackets), pths (parentheses). lenv function simplifies environment creation automatically generating \begin \end statements. second argument accepts list vector element represents separate line. example, equation alternatively formatted : d⟨V,W⟩dt==⟨DVdt,W⟩+⟨V,DWdt⟩\begin{align*}\frac{ d \langle V , W \rangle }{ dt } &=\\&= \langle \frac{ D V }{ dt } , W \rangle + \langle V , \frac{ D W }{ dt } \rangle\end{align*} package also provides il function, wraps expressions dollar signs inline mathematical content.
code: lenv(   "align*",   c(     lsymb(ddt(inner(vf1, vf2)), "&=\\\\"),     lsymb("&=", inner(cov.der(vf1), vf2) + inner(vf1, cov.der(vf2)))   ) ) |> cat()
